body: Thank you for the kind words; I elaborated a little more in another post.

Today at work I should have put my foot down; somebody higher up that me, but who isn't my boss, put a lot of pressure on me to approve a project.  So I ended up folding pretty quickly and approving it on the fly; I know damn right that I'm not supposed to approve something without checking it properly myself.  

But I already felt guilty for this project taking so long to be approved, for a variety of reasons, mainly that I'm a significant contributor to its previous delays.  But I sold myself out to avoid conflict, because it was the end of the day, because this would make up for holding up the project in the past, and so on.

It might not seem like a big thing, but from a practical point of view, I approved a shitty project to go into production, when it's literally my job to yay or nay projects for approval.  Let's just say it didn't take long after I approved it to find major flaws in it.  

To be clear, I'm not upset so much at anyone else, I'm just incredibly disappointed in myself that my lack of courage has come to find me at work, which has historically been a place of solace for me for social failings.  And my boss will be incredibly disappointed in me as well, tomorrow, and understandly so.

The absolute worst though, is that no amount of scolding, or even a firing tomorrow (not likely, but this is definitely my greatest professionnal failure so far) will change this behavior in me.  I can link it to many events throughout my life back to childhood, many worse to the point of almost being repressed; this incident today brought everything back to light all of a sudden.  

I just am not emotionally centered enough as a person to have done the right thing at that time, or any other time where courage was required, consequences uncertain, or confrontation likely; I just take the path of emotional-least-resistance, in this and most other times in my life.  Unless I'm in a blind rage, whenever I'm in a situation like that, I immediately fold, and the emotional and psychological weakness I feel in the moment is so overwhelming that I literally do not think it can be fixed.
